messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: scaled_inv_chi_square, sd or variance?
parts:
Hello,

I would like a confirmation, on which has to be used

1) standard_deviation ~  scaled_inv_chi_square(... , ...)

OR

2) standard_deviation^2 ~  scaled_inv_chi_square(... , ...)

If I use 2, a Jacobian warning is produced

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    pow_ex_sd[g] ~ scaled_inv_chi_square(...)


Thanks a lot.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] scaled_inv_chi_square, sd or variance?
parts:
Hi Stefano,

I don't understand your question. Neither *has* to be used -- you should use what is best for creating a statistical model.

Regarding the Jacobian warning, #2 will generate the warning. That warning SHOULD NOT be ignored in this case.


Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] scaled_inv_chi_square, sd or variance?
parts:
On Friday, December 2, 2016 at 2:01:34 AM UTC-5, Stefano wrote:
usually the variance (standard deviation ^2) is modeled as random variable with scaled_inv_chi_square. Can you confirm this general knowledge?

I think the only way in which the scaled inverse chi-squared distribution is used is with normal mixtures, in which case it pertains to the variance. But then you might as well use the Student t distribution.
If this is true, I would square my standard deviation, (there is no example in the reference guide). If so what Jacobian adjustment should I use?

Just make the primitive parameter be a variance rather than a standard deviation and then there is no need for a Jacobian adjustment.

Ben

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] scaled_inv_chi_square, sd or variance?
parts:
On Friday, December 2, 2016 at 9:01:34 AM UTC+2, Stefano wrote:
usually the variance (standard deviation ^2) is modeled as random variable with scaled_inv_chi_square. Can you confirm this general knowledge?

For variance parameter in a normal model scaled_inv_chi_square is a conjugate prior, which is useful for Gibbs sampling or partial analytic marginalisation, but HMC/NUTS can handle non-conjugate priors as easily as conugate priors, so there is no need to restrict the prior shape. Instead choose the prior based on what you know.  Nowdays it's rare to see scaled_inv_chi_square prior used in Stan models. See  also the discussion of priors at Stan prior choice wiki https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Prior-Choice-Recommendations

Aki
